title: Relative product theorem
statement:
Use the standing field, coefficient categories and operations of [sk-def-sf-operations]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_{p_0^a}$, $a\geq1$, $\ell\ne p_0$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n,\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Integral pullbacks and tensors are completed; rational and algebraically closed coefficients use the specified scalar localization and common finite stages. Let $B$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, let $f:X\to B$ and $g:Y\to B$ be
separated of finite type, let $p,q$ be the projections of $X\times_BY$, so
that $f\times_Bg=g\circ q=f\circ p$, and put
$K\boxtimes L=p^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda q^*L$ for $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$,
$L\in\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$. Define the *relative Künneth map*
$\kappa^{\mathrm{rel}}_{K,L}$ as the composite

$$
\begin{aligned}
R(f\times_Bg)_!\bigl(K\boxtimes L\bigr)
&\xrightarrow{\ \alpha_{g,q}^{-1}\ }Rg_!Rq_!\bigl(p^*K\otimes^L q^*L\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\ Rg_!(\operatorname{PF}_{q,p^*K,L})^{-1}\ }
Rg_!\bigl(Rq_!p^*K\otimes^L L\bigr)\\
&\xrightarrow{\ Rg_!(\operatorname{Ex}_!^{-1}\otimes1)\ }
Rg_!\bigl(Lg^*Rf_!K\otimes^L L\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\ Rg_!(\sigma)\ }
Rg_!\bigl(L\otimes^L Lg^*Rf_!K\bigr)\\
&\xrightarrow{\ (\operatorname{PF}_{g,L,Rf_!K})^{-1}\ }
Rg_!L\otimes^L_\Lambda Rf_!K
\xrightarrow{\ \sigma\ }Rf_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda Rg_!L ,
\end{aligned}
$$

where $\alpha_{g,q}$ is the composition isomorphism of
[thm-sf-comp-composition] at finite coefficients and its completed and transported forms on the domains of [fix-lem-exchanges], $\operatorname{PF}$ the projection
transformation and $\operatorname{Ex}_!:Lg^*Rf_!\to Rq_!Lp^*$ the exchange
transformation of [sk-def-sf-exchanges] for the Cartesian square
$(p,q,f,g)$, and $\sigma$ the symmetry of $\otimes^L$; the second variable
$Rf_!K$ of $\operatorname{PF}_{g,L,Rf_!K}$ lies in $\Dctf(B,\Lambda)$, as the
typing of [sk-def-sf-exchanges] requires, by [thm-sf-ctf-stability]. Then every arrow is an isomorphism
([thm-sf-comp-composition], [sk-rem-sf-pf-done],
[fix-lem-exchanges]), so

$$
\kappa^{\mathrm{rel}}_{K,L}:R(f\times_Bg)_!\bigl(K\boxtimes L\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
Rf_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda Rg_!L
$$

is an isomorphism in the ambient category $D^+(B,\Lambda)$, natural in $K$ and
$L$, compatible with finite reduction, scalar extension, and with the
identifications $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ for proper $f$. Moreover
$\kappa^{\mathrm{rel}}$ is coherent: (i) *symmetry* — under the swap
$X\times_BY\cong Y\times_BX$ and $\sigma$, $\kappa^{\mathrm{rel}}_{L,K}$
corresponds to $\sigma\circ\kappa^{\mathrm{rel}}_{K,L}$ (with the Koszul
signs of $\sigma$); (ii) *triple products* — for a third
separated finite-type $h:W\to B$ and $M\in\Dctf(W,\Lambda)$ the two iterated isomorphisms
$R(f\times_Bg\times_Bh)_!(K\boxtimes L\boxtimes M)\cong
Rf_!K\otimes^LRg_!L\otimes^LRh_!M$ agree after the associativity of
$\otimes^L$; (iii) *base change* — for $b:B'\to B$ with $B'$ a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $Lb^*$ of
$\kappa^{\mathrm{rel}}_{K,L}$ is $\kappa^{\mathrm{rel}}$ of the base-changed
data, through $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ for $f$, $g$, $f\times_Bg$ and the
monoidality of $Lb^*$; (iv) *projection formula* — for $Y=B$,
$g=\mathrm{id}_B$ one has $\kappa^{\mathrm{rel}}_{K,L}=
\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}^{-1}$. For $B=\mathrm{Spec}\,k$ and closed
immersions $i_Z:Z\hookrightarrow X$, $i_W:W\hookrightarrow Y$ it gives the
compact-support product on the closed subschemes
$\RG_c(Z,i_Z^*K)\otimes^L_\Lambda\RG_c(W,i_W^*L)\cong
\RG_c\bigl(Z\times_kW,(i_Z\times i_W)^*(K\boxtimes L)\bigr)$; More generally, over
any $B$ as above, for closed immersions $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$,
$j:W\hookrightarrow Y$, with $i\times_Bj:Z\times_BW\hookrightarrow X\times_BY$
and $h=f\times_Bg$, there is a supported product isomorphism

$$
Rf_!\bigl(i_*i^*K\bigr)\otimes^L_{\Lambda_B}Rg_!\bigl(j_*j^*L\bigr)\cong
Rh_!\bigl((i\times_Bj)_*(i\times_Bj)^*(K\boxtimes L)\bigr).
$$

Cohomology with
supports $\RG_Z(X,K)=\RG(Z,Ri_Z^!K)$ is a different object and is not
asserted here.

proof.text: First instantiate the abstract framework used by the existing expanded theorem, rather than assuming an unproved datum merely because the operations have been defined. The concrete package [prop-functor-package] supplies compact-support composition and proper coincidence (clause 3), compact-support base change (clause 4), projection (clause 5), and coefficient comparisons (clauses 1--2 and the concluding coherence assertion); its last paragraph supplies constructible exceptional adjunction and geometric biduality. The ordinary adjunction with its pasted units and counits is [fix-prop-adjunctions](1),(3), and the comparison coherence is [fix-prop-coherence]. These statements, restricted to their finite-Tor domains, give the clauses (A1)--(A6) required by [def-sf-datum] for the concrete coefficient operations. No unrestricted ambient exceptional adjoint is required. We use this established concrete instance solely to discharge the framework hypothesis of the already-existing formal results below; it is not an extra hypothesis on this theorem. The existing expanded theorem [thm-sf-kunneth-relative] is in this very unit and uses exactly this ordered canonical composite: inverse composition, inverse projection for $q$, inverse exchange for $(p,q,f,g)$, symmetry, inverse projection for $g$, symmetry. Its statement gives invertibility, naturality, finite reduction, scalar extension and the proper identifications for these separated finite-type maps and finite-Tor inputs. Apply it to the concrete datum just specified and to $f,g,K,L$. Its canonical map, not an unspecified isomorphism, is the displayed map here.

source.place: Four arrows (1)--(4), naturality and coefficient/proper compatibility

proof.text: Apply the existing coherence lemma [lem-sf-kunneth-coherence] to the same canonical composite. Its clauses (i), (ii), (iii), (iv) assert respectively the signed swap identity, agreement of the two triple products after the canonical associators, base change through the three compact-support exchanges and monoidal pullback, and the identity-factor projection formula. These are exactly the four coherence assertions here. The third map $h$ has the separated finite-type hypothesis required in clause (ii); clause (iii) is used only for a separated finite-type $B'$, so all corners remain in the specified categories. Both existing nodes use the standing six-functor framework and canonical coefficient comparisons; no assertion about arbitrary discrete integral etale coefficients is made.

For $B=\operatorname{Spec} k$, the closed-subscheme compact-support conclusion is already explicitly the final displayed conclusion of [thm-sf-kunneth-relative]. Apply it to $i_Z,i_W,K,L$ and invert the relative map as in that display. Its statement identifies the pullback of the external product with the external product of the restrictions and identifies the output with coefficient cohomology. Hence it proves the claimed $\RGamma_c$ formula at each of the four coefficient stages. This is ordinary restriction to the closed subschemes, with no extraordinary restriction.

For the general supported product put $A=Li^*K$, $C=Lj^*L$, $T=X\times_BY$, $U=Z\times_BY$, $V=X\times_BW$, and $D=Z\times_BW$. Let $a:U\to T$, $b:V\to T$, $c:D\to U$, $d:D\to V$ be the natural maps; then the square $(c,d,a,b)$ is Cartesian and $r=ac=bd=i\times_Bj$. Each of $a,b,c,d$ is a base change of $i$ or $j$, hence is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]; their composite $r$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp]. All these maps are proper and separated finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. The projections are separated finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. All sources are separated finite-type $k$-schemes: composites of separated morphisms are separated and composites of morphisms locally of finite type are locally of finite type by clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], and a composite of quasi-compact morphisms is quasi-compact because the preimage of a quasi-compact open under the second map is quasi-compact, hence has quasi-compact preimage under the first.

The restriction objects $A,C$, the direct images $Ri_*A,Rj_*C$, their pullbacks to $T$, and all tensors used next lie in the finite-Tor constructible domains. At finite coefficients these are clauses (i), (iii), (ii) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability], respectively. At integral coefficients, pullback and completed tensor preserve bounded constructibility by [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible], and direct image does so by [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible]; clause (vii) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability] identifies integral bounded constructibility with the finite-Tor category. The rational and common-stage versions follow from the explicit objectwise operations and linear extension in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the coefficient-passage clauses of stability. At finite coefficients [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) supplies the etale-origin witnesses needed for compact support and base change. Use the same statement on every finite reduction of integral inputs. Thus the following proper base changes are on witnessed finite or completed/transported domains, not arbitrary pro-etale complexes.

source.place: Supported-product paragraph: preservation for the closed-immersion inputs

proof.text: Write $u:U\to Z$, $v:V\to W$. Proper base change gives $Lp^*Ri_*A\cong Ra_*Lu^*A$, $Lq^*Rj_*C\cong Rb_*Lv^*C$, and $La^*Rb_*Lv^*C\cong Rc_*Ld^*Lv^*C$. At finite coefficients these are compact-support base change [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] through the proper identification [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence]. Integrally use [thm-cbc-complete-proetale], and rationally and at the common stage [thm-cbc-finite-extension], [thm-cbc-qbar], with the proper compactification (open factor the identity). All schemes are noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] over the field, and finite-dimensional by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]; $\ell$ is invertible because $\ell\ne p_0$. The witnessed and constructible hypotheses were checked in step 5. Therefore each of these three displayed proper base-change maps is available at the coefficient stage under consideration.

source.place: Supported-product paragraph: base change for the closed immersions

proof.text:
Now abbreviate $A_U=Lu^*A$ and $C_V=Lv^*C$. The three comparisons of step 6 and the proper projection formula [fix-prop-projection-formula], read in the appropriate direction and using tensor symmetry, give the explicit calculation
$$
\begin{aligned}
Lp^*Ri_*A\otimes^L Lq^*Rj_*C
&\cong Ra_*A_U\otimes^L Rb_*C_V\\
&\cong Ra_*\bigl(A_U\otimes^L La^*Rb_*C_V\bigr)\\
&\cong Ra_*\bigl(A_U\otimes^L Rc_*Ld^*C_V\bigr)\\
&\cong Ra_*Rc_*\bigl(Lc^*A_U\otimes^L Ld^*C_V\bigr)\\
&\cong Rr_*\bigl(Lz^*A\otimes^L Lw^*C\bigr)\\
&\cong Rr_*Lr^*\bigl(K\boxtimes L\bigr).
\end{aligned}
$$
Here $z:D\to Z$, $w:D\to W$ are the projections. The penultimate comparison is the ordinary direct-image composition [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition]. For the last one use monoidal pullback and its composition comparison [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], together with $p\circ r=i\circ z$ and $q\circ r=j\circ w$. Projection for the proper $a,c$ is the direct-image instance of the cited compact-support projection formula. All its second variables are finite-Tor by step 5. This is a few-line application of already cited statements, so the exterior-product identity is a proof step, not a new node.

source.place: Supported-product paragraph: exterior product of extensions by zero

proof.text:
Apply the already established relative formula of [thm-sf-kunneth-relative] to $Ri_*Li^*K$ and $Rj_*Lj^*L$, which satisfy its finite-Tor hypotheses by step 5. Invert it and apply $Rh_!$ to the final isomorphism of step 7. The result is exactly
$$Rf_!(Ri_*Li^*K)\otimes^L Rg_!(Rj_*Lj^*L)\cong Rh_!Rr_*Lr^*\bigl(K\boxtimes L\bigr).$$
This is the asserted supported product, with the conventional $i_*,j_*,r_*$ notation for closed-immersion extension. The field compact-support interpretation is step 3. The separate $\RGamma_Z(X,K)=\RGamma(Z,Ri_Z^!K)$ object in the statement is not used or identified with these restrictions.

Filled the standing coefficient conventions and corrected the out-of-domain base-change quantifier. Proved the general supported product by a Cartesian factorization, three proper base-change comparisons, two projection formulas, and ordinary pushforward composition; the earlier proposed exterior-product child is elementary from these existing nodes and was removed. No new nodes. All search entries are from the actual msearch log; all cited statements have verbatim citations.
